summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for right upper quadrant abdominal pain. She presented after an incomplete dialysis session with elevated potassium and blood glucose. Imaging showed stable moderate ascites, gallbladder wall edema, and findings suggestive of hepatic congestion likely due to cardiac etiology. A pelvic ultrasound ruled out an adnexal mass previously noted on CT. Her pain was managed conservatively, insulin regimen was optimized, and hyperkalemia resolved with dialysis. She improved clinically and was discharged home with plans for outpatient follow-up in cardiology, gastroenterology, and endocrinology, along with a liver MRI to evaluate chronic congestion.
